source_book: NCERT Chemistry Class 11 (states of matter — see caveat) + Cambridge IGCSE / IB DP / AP / A-level kinetic particle theory

real_world_anchor.primary: Block the outlet of a bicycle pump and push: the handle fights back, harder the further you go. That resistance is the whole story here — you are squeezing the same air into less space, so its particles strike the walls more often each second, and 'more hits per second' is what pressure is. (The pump also warms up, which is a second effect from the moving handle doing work on the air; this simulation holds the temperature fixed so the squeeze can be seen on its own.)
real_world_anchor.why_it_matters: Pressure, temperature and volume stop being three symbols in a formula and become one picture of particles hitting walls — which is what makes the gas laws, reaction rates and equilibrium all readable later.

formulas.mean_kinetic_energy: average kinetic energy per particle is proportional to absolute temperature
formulas.pressure_origin: pressure = total wall impulse per unit wall length per unit time
formulas.ideal_gas_law: P V = N k T (dilute limit)

constraints: Absolute temperature is never negative; the temperature slider is floored at 150 K.
Collisions conserve momentum and kinetic energy exactly (perfectly elastic).
Particle count is conserved — no particle is created or destroyed during a state.

aha_moment.statement: One temperature does not mean one speed — there is always a spread.

scene_composition.role: the sealed container of gas — the apparatus that persists in every state
120 hard discs in constant random motion, colliding elastically
the four rigid walls the particles rebound from

tts_sentences.text_en: Its particles are never still — they fly in straight lines, bounce off each other, and change direction constantly.
Nothing is pushing them. This motion is simply what matter does.

scene_composition.role: same apparatus, same home pose
the same particles, now visibly faster at the higher temperature
live temperature readout in kelvin with a tracking bar (Rule 33d)

misconception_watch.belief: Temperature is a substance — heat flows into the gas and sits there.
misconception_watch.visual_counter: the same particles visibly speed up together as the thermometer climbs — nothing is added to the box
misconception_watch.one_line_fix: temperature is not stuff inside the gas; it is how fast its particles already move.

tts_sentences.text_en: Now raise the temperature. Watch the particles speed up together.
Temperature is not a substance that flows in — it is a direct measure of how much kinetic energy the average particle carries.

scene_composition.role: same apparatus, back at the baseline temperature
particles striking the walls — each impact is one contribution to pressure
live pressure readout summed from wall impulses, with a tracking bar
collisions per second — the real number behind the gauge (Rule 33c)

misconception_watch.belief: Pressure is a substance pressing outward, like air packed against the wall.
misconception_watch.visual_counter: each wall strike registers on the gauge; the collisions-per-second counter shows the real number behind it
misconception_watch.one_line_fix: pressure is not a substance pressing out — it is billions of separate impacts, added up.

tts_sentences.text_en: Every particle that strikes a wall gives it a tiny push.
Add up billions of those impacts each second and you get a steady force on every square metre. Pressure is collisions, counted.

scene_composition.role: the same box, now compressed — the original extent stays on screen as a ghost outline
the moving wall; a closing wall does real work on the particles it rebounds
pressure rises as the volume falls — the same instrument, a new reading
collisions per second climbs with the compression
holds at the same temperature while pressure climbs — the instrument that makes 'speed unchanged' checkable rather than asserted

tts_sentences.text_en: Push the wall in and watch the thermometer.
It does not move: the particles have not changed speed, and none have been added.
Only the box is smaller, so each particle reaches a wall sooner. More hits per second means more pressure.

scene_composition.role: the same gas at the baseline temperature
some particles visibly crawling, others racing across the box
live count of how many particles hold each speed, with the theory curve overlaid
most-probable, average and root-mean-square speeds marked on the same axis

misconception_watch.belief: At a given temperature every particle moves at the same speed — 'the' speed of the gas.
misconception_watch.visual_counter: the histogram fills in live — slow and fast particles counted side by side at one fixed temperature
misconception_watch.one_line_fix: one temperature gives a whole spread of speeds, not a single speed.

tts_sentences.text_en: Here is what surprises most people.
At one temperature the particles do not share one speed. Some crawl, some race, most sit near the middle.
The graph counts them — a spread, never a single value.

scene_composition.role: the same apparatus while the temperature sweeps
pressure climbing as the gas is heated
the temperature driving that climb
pressure times area divided by particle count and temperature — holds steady while both inputs change

tts_sentences.text_en: One relationship ties all of it together.
Multiply pressure by volume, then divide by particle count and by temperature.
The answer holds steady even as you heat the gas — and that steady value is the gas law itself.

scene_composition.role: the live sandbox — every core instrument available at once
pressure responding live to every drag
temperature responding live to every drag
the distribution sliding as the temperature changes
temperature, volume and particle count, all live

tts_sentences.text_en: Your turn. Change the temperature, the volume, and the number of particles, and watch pressure answer.

regeneration_variants.label: Same physics, a different container (a sealed syringe instead of a rigid box)
regeneration_variants.physical_world: A sealed syringe with the nozzle blocked: pressing the plunger compresses the trapped gas and the plunger springs back. The identical kinetic story — smaller volume, more frequent wall impacts, higher pressure — with an apparatus a student can hold.
